top_choice_rationale: P005 (Melitz and Helpman, B041) rests on one identifiable discovery: selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and FDI. It created a reallocation channel for the gains from trade and tied trade theory to firm-level data. Twenty years of theoretical, structural and firm-level work support it. Its main weakness is attribution, since Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made parallel contributions and Helpman's credit is shared with P004. I narrow the citation to selection into exporting and FDI and the resulting reallocation. I hold this lead by a small margin over P001, which has the cleanest attribution among the empirical candidates but carries debated magnitudes and a narrower citation. P004 and P002 follow: both are mature and cleanly attributed, but P004 has a mixed empirical record and P002 has indirect empirical content. P003 is younger and relies on restricted data. I rank no award last because every proposal is credible on the common criteria.
recusal_note: No connection to Melitz, Helpman, Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Grossman, Rubinstein, Wolinsky, Chetty, Hendren or Friedman is apparent from the profile. I frequently co-author with Per Krusell, who supports P004, and have co-authored with Timo Boppart and Richard Friberg, who are committee colleagues. My research on social mobility is thematically related to P003, which I do not prefer. I wrote the round-1 chair summary and my first choice is P005. These ties are disclosed, not adjudicated.
